ACT 1 · THE STORY

How she presented

CASE PRESENTATION

A woman aged 90+ with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis for 12 years (Tue / Thu / Sat), recurrent herpes simplex keratitis, a permanent pacemaker, hypothyroidism and GERD was started on valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily for ocular herpes.

The next evening she developed expressive aphasia, left-sided weakness with a left arm pronator drift, and new visual hallucinations.

She presented to Hospital A with altered mental status. Her blood pressure peaked at 220/80 and she failed her bedside swallow.

ACT 1 · THE SNF

Day 8 at the SNF: both drugs restarted

The next day, both stopped drugs were back on the SNF medication record.

Valacyclovir was first entered “for shingles”, then re-entered “for ocular herpes”.

ganciclovir eye drops, 5×/day × 21 days

Same printer. Same ink. Impossible to miss.

AFTER · STOP-FIRST REDESIGN
ACT 3 · THE SOLUTION

Six rules for a B&W-proof medication page

1 STOP prints first

Before anything else on the medication page.

2 STOP never splits across a page

If the list must break, repeat the STOP box on the next page.

3 Shape codes, not colour

stop

new

changed

same

4 Count strip at the top

“2 STOP · 3 NEW · 3 CHANGED · 4 SAME”

5 Strike-through + “was:” + “WHY stopped”

On every stopped drug. No “duration / filled” on stop rows.

6 Close the loop

“Removed from MAR — RN initials” box, plus an end-of-list total.

ACT 3 · THE SOLUTION

Beyond the paper

System levers, strongest first.

STRONGER

WEAKER

1

Forcing function

Stopped for toxicity → entered as an adverse drug reaction before discharge; travels as a hard stop.

2

Closed loop

Receiver reads back the STOP list [by phone / attestation — mechanism to be decided]; sender confirms.

3

Line 1 of the discharge summary / TOC note

“DO NOT RESTART [drug] — caused [reaction].”

4

Pharmacist-led transition med rec

For SNF discharges on renally cleared high-risk drugs [evidence to be verified].

5

Standardize the template

Across the health system.

ACT 3 · THE SOLUTION

Two lenses

ATOMIC HABITS · LAW 1

Make it obvious.

Make the right action the most visible thing on the page.

Add friction to the wrong action — restarting.

STOP: the loudest thing on the page.

CYBERNETICS · OPEN VS CLOSED LOOP

Today we print and hope.

A system without feedback can’t correct itself. Add the read-back.

Open loop

PrintHopeno feedback

Closed loop

SendRead backConfirm
IS THIS JUST HOSPITAL A?

We print ours the same way

Our own discharge paperwork prints medications the same way. Three take-homes:

1

In print, STOP must be the loudest thing on the page — and never on the next page.

2

A drug stopped for toxicity must be recorded as an adverse reaction, or the next system can’t protect the patient.

3

Every handoff needs a feedback loop, not just a fax.

M&M · INTERNAL MEDICINE
